title: Halley's Comet
subtitle: Once in a lifetime
description:
Episode 36 of a daily journey through the universe. ☄️
We chase Halley's Comet: a dirty snowball that returns every 76 years, the 1986 spacecraft flyby, its return in 2061, and the two meteor showers its dust creates every year.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 37: Next stop, the International Space Station.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

segments.text: Episode thirty-six. Next stop... Halley's Comet.
A comet is a dirty snowball of ice and dust. Near the Sun, it heats up and grows a glowing tail.
segments.headline: A cosmic snowball

segments.text: Halley's Comet returns about every seventy-six years.
Its last visit was in nineteen eighty-six. Spacecraft flew past and photographed its dark, potato-shaped core.
segments.headline: Last seen: 1986

segments.text: It comes back in twenty sixty-one. Mark your calendar.
And every year, Earth passes through its leftover dust. That creates two meteor showers, in May and October.
segments.headline: Its dust becomes shooting stars

segments.text: Tomorrow, we visit the only home humans have in space. Next stop: the International Space Station. Follow, so you don't miss episode thirty-seven.
